metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model delays response — anticipate early reversal and adjust forecast to rise sooner.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral — add 1–2% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often overestimates momentum — cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to lag — forecast should start rising 1–2 days earlier than observed trend.
- In high-sentiment environments, model often ignores volatility — increase forecast variance by 1–2% to reflect sentiment-driven noise.
